rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at mid temperature to reveal the full retention window and whether any compounds are missing by 42 min. This should place most peaks inside the gradient and give a useful first map for narrowing the phi window and adjusting slope in later injections.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the only objective is to pull the last peak under 10 min while keeping every peak inside the gradient. The observed elution window corresponds roughly to phi_e about 0.09 to 0.38, so a trimmed, steeper gradient should preserve resolution margin and shorten the run substantially.

Resolution still has comfortable margin, so push retention down further with a slightly steeper, slightly stronger method and a modest temperature increase to target t_last below 10 min. The critical cluster is around peaks 5–7, but with min R still above 2 there is room to trade some resolution for speed.

The loss came from selectivity, not time: the critical 6/7 pair collapsed when temperature was raised. Keep the fast gradient that nearly gets t_last under 10 min, but lower T to recover that pair while hopefully retaining most of the speed gain.

The 10 min gradient is too steep for the middle cluster at both 35 and 45 C, while 12 min at 40 C was fully resolved. Keep the favorable 40 C selectivity and test whether a slightly stronger, still fast method can shave enough retention to reach t_last near 10 min without collapsing the critical pairs.

You already have the maximum CRF, so this is only a robustness probe around the optimum. A slightly stronger endpoint may shorten the last peak further while likely preserving full resolution, testing whether the optimum sits on a small plateau.

The endpoint increase hurt the critical 6/7 pair, so keep phi1 at 0.65 and instead test whether a shorter gradient alone can still stay on the CRF=1 plateau. This directly probes how much slope margin remains around the optimum while preserving the favorable selectivity at 40 C.

Since steepening in time hurt the 6/7 pair, test a slightly higher starting organic instead to shorten the run while keeping the same endpoint and gradient time. The first peak is still well retained, so raising phi0 may reduce overall retention yet preserve selectivity better than shortening tG or raising phi1.

Raising phi0 from 0.10 to 0.15 preserved full resolution and improved both speed and the critical 6/7 margin, so test one more increment upward. The first peak should still not be unretained, and this may reveal a broader CRF=1 plateau with a faster method.

At phi0 0.15 and 10 min there is a bit more resolution margin than at the original optimum, so use that margin to shorten tG rather than raise phi0 further. This tests whether a faster method can remain on the CRF=1 plateau while avoiding the first-peak compression seen at phi0 0.20.

The CRF=1 methods suggest the plateau is narrow in slope, and increasing phi0 helped more than increasing phi1. Lowering phi1 slightly while keeping phi0 0.15 and tG 10 may preserve or even improve the critical 6/7 separation while still keeping the last peak under 10 min.

You already have CRF 1.000, so this is a robustness map on the high-organic/high-time side of the optimum. Compared with 0.15/0.65/10, a slightly longer but stronger gradient should show whether the fully resolved plateau extends toward gentler slope with shorter hold dependence for the last peak.

The data show 6/7 is the limiting pair and responds strongly to effective gradient steepness. This condition keeps the beneficial higher phi0 but offsets the too-steep 8 min slope by widening the gradient window, probing whether that pair can stay at or above 1.5 while retaining a very short run.

Around 40 C the best region is already mapped, so test whether the alternate CRF=1 composition at phi0 0.15 shifts favorably with temperature. Since 6/7 is the limiting pair and temperature changed the critical pairing before, this checks whether a modest T increase can maintain full resolution at this higher phi0 setting.

Temperature clearly perturbs the critical selectivity, and 45 C strongly worsened the 6/7 pair. Test the opposite direction from the successful 0.15/0.65/10/40 method to see whether slightly lower temperature strengthens the limiting pair while potentially remaining under 10 min.

The best score is already reached, so use remaining runs to map the robustness boundary in the other direction for phi0. Lowering phi0 from the CRF=1 region should show whether extra low-organic focusing helps or hurts the critical mid-cluster while keeping the same successful tG, phi1, and T.

The optimum appears to lie on a narrow ridge in slope/selectivity, with phi0 0.15 slightly strengthening the critical 6/7 pair relative to phi0 0.10. Test a stronger endpoint at the same tG and T to define the upper phi1 robustness boundary from the CRF=1 method at 0.15/0.65/10/40.

The best score is already secured, so use one remaining probe to map the temperature robustness boundary above 45 C for the original optimum composition. Since higher temperature strongly affects the limiting 6/7 selectivity, this will confirm how sharply the CRF=1 region collapses with T.

High temperature sharply changes selectivity, but part of that loss may be recoverable with a shallower gradient. This run tests whether extra gradient time at 45 C can restore the critical 6/7 separation while keeping the last peak near 10 min, mapping a possible alternative optimum ridge.

At 40 C, lowering phi1 improved the critical 6/7 pair but pushed the last peak just past 10 min when phi0 was 0.15. Using the original lower phi0 with a 12 min gradient checks whether the balance shifts enough to reveal another fully resolved region near the low-phi1 boundary.

At 0.20/0.65/10 the first peak became quite early and the critical 6/7 pair was only slightly below target, while at 0.15/0.60/10 the pair improved but the last peak was too late. Combining higher phi0 with lower phi1 should steepen the window less than raising phi1 and may keep t_last below 10 while restoring the limiting pair.

At 0.20/0.60/10 the critical pair is comfortably resolved but the last peak is just over 10 min, so shorten retention with a shorter run while using lower temperature to counter the usual loss of 6/7 selectivity from steeper conditions. This tests whether time and temperature can trade off to keep full resolution and pull t_last below 10.

The 0.20/0.60/8/35 run showed the critical pair switched from 6/7 to 5/6, confirming strong temperature-driven selectivity changes. Testing the opposite temperature extreme at the same fast composition maps whether this setting can regain separation through a different selectivity pattern while keeping the run very short.

The 0.20/0.60/10/40 method was fully resolved but just missed the 10 min target, so lengthening tG there is not for score but to confirm the slope sensitivity of the critical 6/7 pair at this alternate composition. This gives a cleaner robustness bracket against the failed 8 min runs and the near-optimal 10 min run.

For the final run, probe the remaining untested corner near the optimum: low phi0 with low phi1 at the successful 10 min, 40 C settings. Lower phi0 slightly weakened the 6/7 pair at phi1 0.65, while lower phi1 tends to strengthen it but lengthen the run, so this run cleanly maps that tradeoff around the best region.
